title: extractSubset
body:
## extractSubset

Extracts a volume of interest from structured data (image data, rectilinear or structured grid) by an IJK point-index range, optionally keeping every n-th index. The output keeps the input's structured type, so it stays compact and works with structured filters. Use it to crop a structured block or image by index; use a clip for geometric cuts or unstructured meshes.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Indices are in the input's extent space, which need not start at 0; inspect the input extent before choosing the range.

Native constructor: `ExtractSubset`. Identity: `curated binding`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. Accepted data: image data (uniform rectilinear grids) (vtkImageData); rectilinear grids (vtkRectilinearGrid); structured points (image data) (vtkStructuredPoints); curvilinear structured grids (vtkStructuredGrid). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkImageData","vtkRectilinearGrid","vtkStructuredPoints","vtkStructuredGrid"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `extent` | This property specifies the minimum and maximum point indices along each of the I, J, and K axes; these values indicate the volume of interest (VOI). The output will have the (I,J,K) extent specified here. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"integer"},"minItems":6,"maxItems":6}` | `required` | `[1,1,1,1,1,1]` |
| `rateI` | This property indicates the sampling rate in the I dimension. A value greater than 1 results in subsampling; every nth index will be included in the output. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":1}` | `1` | `1` |
| `rateJ` | This property indicates the sampling rate in the J dimension. A value greater than 1 results in subsampling; every nth index will be included in the output. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":1}` | `1` | `1` |
| `rateK` | This property indicates the sampling rate in the K dimension. A value greater than 1 results in subsampling; every nth index will be included in the output. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":1}` | `1` | `1` |
| `includeBoundary` | If the value of this property is 1, then if the sample rate in any dimension is greater than 1, the boundary indices of the input dataset will be passed to the output even if the boundary extent is not an even multiple of the sample rate in a given dimension. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `true` | `true` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "extractSubset",
  "inputs": {
    "input": "UPSTREAM_input"
  },
  "options": {
    "extent": [
      1,
      1,
      1,
      1,
      1,
      1
    ]
  }
}
```
